s1.syndrome_frame: Episodic tachycardia in a pregnant patient
salient_findings: Regular nonexertional episodic palpitations
Visible neck pulsation
Regular cannon waves on jugular venous pulsations
Variable first heart sound on auscultation
Regular narrow QRS tachycardia on ECG
key_facts: Patient is a primigravid in their 20s
Patient is in the eighth month of gestation
Palpitations last for a few minutes and subside spontaneously
No associated sweating, syncope, dyspnoea, orthopnoea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea
Blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg
Heart rate is 120 beats/min
General examination is unremarkable
Laboratory tests are within normal limits
2-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography shows good biventricular function and normally functioning valves
ECG shows regular narrow QRS tachycardia with a ventricular rate of 103-125 beats/min

shortlist.label: Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Regular narrow QRS tachycardia with a ventricular rate of 103-125 beats/min and regular P waves evident marching onto QRS complexes

shortlist.label: Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Episodic palpitations and regular narrow QRS tachycardia are consistent with AVNRT

shortlist.label: Atrial Flutter
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of regular narrow QRS tachycardia, although less likely given the presence of regular P waves

shortlist.label: Focal Atrial Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of narrow QRS tachycardia, although less likely given the regularity of the P waves

shortlist.label: Junctional Ectopic Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of narrow QRS tachycardia, although less likely given the presence of regular P waves and the clinical context

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG shows regular narrow QRS tachycardia with a ventricular rate of 103-125 beats/min, which is consistent with supraventricular tachycardia. The presence of regular P waves marching onto QRS complexes at a rate of 100-125 beats/min with varying PR intervals also supports this diagnosis. Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia is a common cause of paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia, especially in young women.

rejected.label: Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia
rejected.why: Too broad, as it encompasses several specific diagnoses including Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia

rejected.label: Atrial Flutter
rejected.why: Typically characterized by a regular, rapid atrial rhythm with a fixed block, which is not evident in the ECG description

rejected.label: Focal Atrial Tachycardia
rejected.why: Usually presents with an irregular rhythm and P wave morphology that is different from sinus rhythm, not seen in this case

rejected.label: Junctional Ectopic Tachycardia
rejected.why: Typically presents with a narrow QRS complex tachycardia and retrograde P waves, which are not described in the ECG findings
